stories.stat_label: giant insects released into the wild
stories.headline: The world's heaviest insect is officially bouncing back
stories.summary: A breeding programme has released 11,000 wētāpunga, and the species is now listed as increasing. Females can weigh as much as a mouse and grow up to 10 cm long.
stories.why: Predators and lost habitat had pushed this giant insect to the brink.

stories.headline: A solar-powered ambulance drove 800+ km across Kenya
stories.summary: Dutch students built Stella Juva, billed as the 1st solar ambulance. It carries vaccines, an ultrasound and X-ray gear, and is being trialled in Kenya with Amref Health Africa.
stories.why: It could bring a clinic to villages with no power or fuel.

stories.headline: A prosthetist turns old bike parts into free-to-copy legs
stories.summary: Ben Hogan's Project Bike Leg makes prosthetic legs almost entirely from used bike parts. He taught students in Ghana to build them and isn't patenting the design.
stories.why: Low-cost legs could reach amputees who can't afford one.

stories.headline: 368 farmers gave up land so elephants could cross safely
stories.summary: Tanzania's first protected wildlife corridor links savanna and mountain rainforest. Cameras caught 529 elephants using it in 15 months, and 100,000 native trees have been planted.
stories.why: Elephants get their old route back and farmers keep their crops.

fun_fact: Udzungwa elephants occasionally slide down steep slopes on their bums in the rainy season.
